evidence.title: Shock gloves bought by ICE cause intense pain, Army study says

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study
occurrences.quote_span: The participants, several of whom were large-statured men, stopped resisting seconds after officers applied shocks by touching gloves to their skin, and were left with "fatigue, soreness and excessive apprehensiveness to being shocked again," the study found.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study
occurrences.quote_span: The electric jolt does not cause the body to freeze like a Taser shock does, but instead "works by overloading the peripheral nerve endings" of the skin to cause pain, the study said.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study
occurrences.quote_span: "GLOVE provides a boost in confidence to smaller or less trained members," the study found. "Inmate compliance was immediate" compared to other methods, it added.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study
occurrences.quote_span: They did not "significantly change" the time it took to control inmates during escorts but required less effort.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study
occurrences.quote_span: "After experiencing the effects of the GLOVE ... participants stated just seeing the GLOVE was enough to make them want to comply," the authors wrote.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study authors
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: American Oversight statement and Army assessment
occurrences.quote_span: "The military assessment in ICE's own files shows that these gloves can cause 'intense pain' and force compliance. It does not establish that they are safe," said Chioma Chukwu, executive director of American Oversight.
occurrences.speaker: Chioma Chukwu
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study
occurrences.quote_span: Role-playing employees conducted several scenarios with and without the gloves to test their impact, including violent encounters in which inmates were to fight as hard as they could.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study
occurrences.quote_span: The military prison study assessed whether the gloves could be used effectively to forcibly remove combative prisoners from their cells, to respond to disturbances in common areas and to transport uncooperative inmates.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study and Fort Leavenworth exercise records
occurrences.quote_span: The shocks had a profound impact on Army employees who played the role of combative prisoners during the exercise, which took place at the military prison at Fort Leavenworth in Kansas in October 2024.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Army shock glove study
occurrences.quote_span: The study found the devices "increased the efficiency" of teams carrying out forced cell extractions and responding to disturbances by reducing the length of physical encounters, keeping guards from becoming exhausted and preventing injuries.
occurrences.speaker: U.S. Army study
occurrences.subject: U.S. Army shock glove study
